sections.h2: Where does Lenoir County send its property tax bills from?
sections.html:
Bills come from the Lenoir County Tax Department in the administration building at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston, phone 252-527-7174. Plan a visit between 8:30 and 5:00 any weekday.

One office carries several jobs. It lists and appraises real estate, keeps ownership and transfer records, tracks exemptions, exclusions and deferrals, and mails the bills. It also bills the special districts layered over the county: fire districts, municipal service districts and drainage districts. Solid waste fees, privilege licenses and permits to move mobile homes run through the same counter.

The county website links to online bill viewing and payment, real property records, GIS maps, a scheduler for real property appeals, and listing forms for business and individual personal property. A seller checking a bill before closing can look there first and then phone for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: How does the tax calendar work for a Lenoir County bill?
sections.html:
A bill is due on September 1, yet it costs nothing extra until January 6. Past that day, 2 percent interest is charged through February 1, then 3/4 percent a month, counting part of a month as a whole one.

Calendar rules that shape a Lenoir County tax year, with the statute for each
StepWhat the law saysWhere to read it
ListingOpens the first business day of January, closes January 31G.S. 105-307
Payment dateSeptember 1 of the fiscal year for which the tax is leviedG.S. 105-360
Last interest-free dayThe day before January 6G.S. 105-360
Review board convenesFirst sitting falls between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of MayG.S. 105-322
Next appeal levelWritten notice of appeal to the state commission within a month of the mailed rulingG.S. 105-290

A mailed payment is dated by its postmark.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lenoir County property value?
sections.html:
Real estate appeals in this county are heard by its Board of Equalization and Review. The 2026 window ended on April 23, 2026, when the board adjourned. Per the county, the 2027 window opens on January 1, 2027.

This quasi-judicial board hears disputes over how real estate and personal property were listed and appraised, plus exemption applications, exclusion requests and present-use classifications, all under G.S. 105-322.

Timing is strict: ask for a hearing, by letter or in person, before the board adjourns. A written decision follows within 30 days of adjournment. Someone still unhappy can file notice with the state Property Tax Commission inside 30 days of the mailing date, stating the grounds and sending a copy to the assessor. The county site offers a form for scheduling a real property appeal.

sections.h2: When did Lenoir County last revalue property?
sections.html:
Lenoir County's own page says assessed values held steady after the reappraisal effective January 1, 2017, and it described the next one as effective January 1, 2025. North Carolina law sets the outside limit at eight years between reappraisals of real property.

In between, a value changes only when the property does, for example through new construction or a removed building. During a reappraisal, certified appraisers visit parcels, confirm characteristics and study sales and costs so every property is measured as of the same date.

Treat the assessed figure as a tax number and not a market price. Weigh it against recent sales when choosing an asking price, and request the current assessed value on your parcel from the office.

sections.h2: What property tax relief programs exist for Lenoir County owners?
sections.html:
Three homestead programs exist statewide, and the county takes the AV-9 application for them. One owner may claim just one of them. File during the listing period; the county must still accept an application up to June 1 before the tax year.

  • Age or disability: protects $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is the larger figure. Applicants must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, and report income no higher than the $38,800 figure NCDOR prints for 2026.
  • Disabled veterans: the program removes $45,000 of appraised value from the tax base. NCDOR's form says no age or income limit applies, and the owner submits Form NCDVA-9 through the assessor.
  • Circuit breaker: limits the bill to 4.0 percent of income at or below the cap, and to 5.0 percent between the cap and 150 percent of it (NCDOR prints $58,200 for 2026). The owner must have owned and lived in the house for five years, and a fresh application is filed yearly. Deferred tax becomes due on a sale.

Farm, horticulture and forest land may qualify for present-use value, which lowers the assessment. Lenoir County has an AV-7 form to request an estimate of deferred taxes, a useful step before selling qualifying land.

sections.h2: What does a Lenoir County landlord or business owner have to list?
sections.html:
Anyone holding personal property tied to a business or other income-producing use must file a Business Personal Property Listing Form during January. The county names machinery, equipment, computers, furniture, fixtures, farm machinery, airplanes, supplies and construction in progress as examples. Rental owners who keep appliances, tools or equipment for their Lenoir County units should read that list.

An account that listed last year receives its form in the mail automatically. If none arrives, the county says it is the owner's job to ask for one during regular office hours. Organizations seeking an exemption from personal property tax must file their application by January 31.

Before December ends, the tax office also mails abstract listings to every taxpayer who listed the year before. Listing real estate for the first time, such as a newly built house, is a call to the Tax Assessor's Office, which can explain what a new owner has to provide.

sections.h2: What happens to Lenoir County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
State law fastens the lien to a parcel as of January 1, so an unpaid balance stays attached to the house until it is paid. At closing, the attorney or title company usually requests the figure from the Lenoir County Tax Department and pays it out of the seller's proceeds.

Personal property works differently. A lien for unpaid personal property tax can reach every parcel the taxpayer owns in that taxing unit, so an old boat or equipment bill may surface against a house. Boats, jet skis, aircraft, mobile homes and unlicensed vehicles are listed each January, with a 10 percent penalty for a late listing.

Real estate follows a permanent listing system in this county. A seller does not relist the house every year unless its value changed.

sections.h2: What happens if Lenoir County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
To collect, the county can file a court action that mirrors a mortgage foreclosure, brought where the property is located. Owners of record, spouses and other lienholders receive notice.

The foreclosure sale is a public auction outside the courthouse. The steps after the bidding are short:

  • A bidder may be asked to put down as much as 20 percent.
  • The commissioner files a report on the sale within three days.
  • Ten days run from the report for anyone to object or raise the bid.
  • A fee of up to 5 percent of the price goes to the commissioner.
  • Before a judge confirms the sale, redemption is possible for whoever pays everything owed on the parcel.

The county tax page names a legal services contact for tax foreclosures. Anyone holding a notice should call the tax office and a legal aid provider promptly.

sections.h2: What are the housing and income figures for Lenoir County?
sections.html:
Lenoir County had an estimated 55,837 residents on July 1, 2025, down from 59,495 in the 2010 census, and it has 27,402 housing units across 399.09 square miles.

Survey data for 2020 to 2024 gives $120,500 as the middle value of a home that its owner occupies. Owner-occupancy stands at 59.2 percent. Rent in the county has a median of $861. Households earn a median $45,143. The poverty rate is 19.1 percent, and people 65 and over make up 22.4 percent of the county.

Monthly owner costs are a median $1,237 with a mortgage and $460 without one. At home values this modest, a tax bill is a real share of yearly housing cost, and back taxes can eat much of a house's equity. Only 131 building permits were issued in 2025, which leaves a resale competing mainly with other older houses.

faqs.q: Which phone number reaches Lenoir County tax staff?
faqs.a: The tax office answers at 252-527-7174, from its Kinston location at 101 North Queen Street, on weekdays from 8:30 until 5:00.

faqs.q: Is the Lenoir County real estate appeal period still open for 2026?
faqs.a: No. It closed April 23, 2026, when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned. The county says the window for 2027 opens January 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Must a Lenoir County homeowner list the house each year?
faqs.a: No. The county runs a permanent listing system for real estate, so a house is relisted only after a change in value. Boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles need a January listing.

faqs.q: What does a late personal property listing cost in Lenoir County?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty. Listings made after the period ending January 31 are charged it, per the county tax page.

faqs.q: Can a house with unpaid Lenoir County tax be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is settled from the seller's proceeds when the sale closes. Ask the tax office for the figure ahead of signing, so it is printed on the settlement statement.
